task.description:
FINAL GATE on the ISS-0440 design (rework 3, commit 06bfa746). You have failed this design three times, each time correctly, and each finding was real -- the third one you verified at Mix's own run_alias/6 source level. Rework 3 was YOUR specified fix, applied. This gate has ONE question.

THE ONE QUESTION: is the Tier 2 qualifier now present, correct, and propagated everywhere the unqualified claim previously stood? CODE-DESIGNER reports applying your wording verbatim to section 1's Tier 2 bullet -- naming the three earlier alias entries and their Mix.raise behaviour, citing the run_alias/6 evidence, and stating the corrected guarantee as 'always detected and recorded whenever CI reaches the linter, which happens unless an earlier alias entry fails first -- in which case Tier 1 still holds (the job goes red) but H1's own check is not what is reported that run.' It then reports propagating it FURTHER than you asked: an umbrella sentence atop 3.5, the qualifier spelled out in full at 3.5's opening AND its closing self-description, at AC1's Mechanism A bullet, and at section 7's guidance for the anti-patterns.md note DOC-UPDATER will write -- that last one because the guidance was itself repeating the unqualified phrasing as instructions for future content. Section 6.4 now cites ISS-0441/GH#851 by id and explains that a required status check on the whole letflow.check job closes the Tier 2 ordering gap too, since it blocks the merge regardless of which alias entry produced the red.
  ORCH verified mechanically: the corrected phrase 'whenever CI reaches the linter' appears 5 times; ISS-0441 is referenced 3 times; the diff is 123 insertions / 65 deletions confined to the design file plus its own handoff.
  YOUR JOB: (i) confirm the qualifier is correct as written and not subtly weaker than what you specified; (ii) confirm NO unqualified restatement survives anywhere -- this is the fourth time this class has been checked, and it hid in a different section each previous time, so sweep rather than spot-check, section 7's DOC-UPDATER guidance and any summary/abstract text included; (iii) confirm the settled items did not move (item 2's --dir/--autofix text, 1.2's closing pointer, section 4's verdicts, section 5's demonstration steps, AC3/AC4/AC5, the 1900-file figure).

CLOSE IT IF IT IS RIGHT. rework_count is at max (3 of 3). If this PASSES, route to ELIXIR-DEV and the run proceeds. If it FAILS, ORCH must escalate rather than dispatch a fourth rework -- so a FAIL here should be reserved for a genuine surviving defect of the same class, not a wording preference, not a newly-invented fourth-order objection, and not thoroughness for its own sake. You have already extracted the real value from this design; three correct FAILs is a good outcome, and a fourth would need to be as well-evidenced as the first three. Equally: if an unqualified claim genuinely still stands somewhere, say so plainly -- passing a design you believe is still overclaiming would be the worst outcome available, given that is the exact failure mode this issue exists to end.

Do not edit lib/ or test/. Complete the handoff with a clear PASS/FAIL and per-item verdicts; on PASS set next_action to route to ELIXIR-DEV. Commit to branch feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903.

result.summary: PASS. Final gate after rework 3 (design commit 06bfa746). This is the fourth check of the same defect class (unqualified structural/detection claims), and unlike the prior three, swept the entire 915-line document section by section rather than spot-checking, per the task's own instruction. No surviving unqualified restatement found anywhere.  ITEM (i) -- the qualifier is correct as written, not weaker than specified. Re-read the exact corrected sentence at section 1's Tier 2 bullet (lines 88-93): word-for-word the sentence I required at the prior gate -- always detected and recorded whenever CI reaches the linter, which happens unless an earlier alias entry fails first, in which case Tier 1 still holds (the job goes red) but H1's own check is not what is reported that run -- plus an additional sentence not required but correct and useful: detection cannot be skipped once the linter is reached, and an earlier-entry failure never produces a false clean reading, it produces a red job for a different, already-detected reason instead. That extra sentence directly forecloses the exact misreading risk this whole finding was about (a short-circuited run being mistaken for an H1 pass) -- strictly stronger than what was asked for, not subtly weaker. The Mix-source citation (run_alias/6, the OptionParser.ParseError-scoped rescue) and the three named alias entries (check_toolchain, check_requirements_registration, check_deferral_staleness) match what I verified independently at the prior gate.  ITEM (ii) -- swept the full document, not spot-checked, since this class hid in a different section each of the three previous times. Grepped for every absolute-strength phrase across the whole file (whenever CI reaches the linter: 5 hits, matching ORCH's count; always detected / always DETECTED / detected and recorded: 9 additional occurrences beyond the 5; plus a second sweep for cannot be skipped / unconditionally / guaranteed / nothing bypasses / every time / impossible, 20+ more hits) and read every one in its surrounding paragraph, not just the matched line. Findings by location: section 1's Tier 2 bullet (line 70) carries the qualifier inline in its own header, not just its body. Section 3.5 opens with an explicit umbrella sentence (lines 514-518) declaring that every always detected and recorded phrase in that section carries section 1's Tier 2 qualifier by reference even where not respelled -- checked this actually covers every instance that follows in the section (lines 522, 529, 540, 571 -- the section runs lines 505-579, confirmed via the next heading at line 580): 522 and 529 spell the qualifier out inline anyway; 540's bare Tier 2 still holds: the violation is still detected and recorded relies on the umbrella and is legitimately covered by it (same pointer technique already accepted for section 1.2 at the prior gate); 571-578 is the section's closing self-description and spells the full qualifier out completely and explicitly, exactly as ORCH described -- confirmed this is not left as the one place it stays implicit. AC1's Mechanism A bullet (lines 665-673) spells the qualifier out fully inline, correctly. AC2 (line 752) uses unconditionally only about Tier 1 (every host's changes are scanned, host-independence), never makes a Tier 2 detection claim -- different meaning, not the same defect. Section 6.4 (line 838) cross-references section 1's Tier 2 bullet rather than restating unqualified, and its own heading now states explicitly that branch protection would close the Tier 2 ordering gap too. Section 7's DOC-UPDATER guidance (item 3, the anti-patterns.md note instructions) now states the three-tier precision explicitly as an instruction for future content and says never as an unqualified always detected -- this is the fourth location's fix and the one most clearly targeted at the failure mode of this defect class recurring in future documentation rather than just in this document. Checked every other section for a claim of the same shape under different wording: sections 0, 1.2, 2/2.1/2.1a, 2.2-2.5, 3/3.1-3.4, 4 (all four candidate verdicts), AC3/AC4/AC5, 6.1-6.3 -- none makes an unqualified Tier-2-shaped claim; AC4's satisfied structurally is about the fix being role-agnostic, a different sense of structural entirely, and was already confirmed byte-identical to the settled rework-1 text, not new. No surviving unqualified restatement found anywhere in the document.  ITEM (iii) -- settled items stayed put, confirmed by direct byte-diff (not just a header- level diff) between the rework-2 (b4ed0a41) and rework-3 (06bfa746) versions of the design file: section 2.1/2.1a (--dir/--autofix text), section 1.2's closing pointer, section 4 (all four candidate verdicts including the hook rejection), section 5's six numbered AC1 demonstration steps, and AC3/AC4/AC5 are all byte-for-byte IDENTICAL across the two versions -- zero diff lines in every one of those five diffs. The 1900-file corpus figure appears at the same three locations in both versions, content unchanged. git diff --stat confirms 123 insertions / 65 deletions in the design file itself, matching ORCH's report exactly; the full commit's other three touched files are handoff/registry bookkeeping, not lib/ or test/.  VERDICT: PASS. The qualifier is correct, not weakened, and propagated everywhere the unqualified claim previously stood or could plausibly recur, confirmed by an exhaustive section-by-section sweep rather than a spot-check. All items settled at the prior three gates remain byte-identical. Route to ELIXIR-DEV.
result.next_action: Route to ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a) -- design is finalized after 3 correct reworks, all four gate rounds' findings resolved. rework_count is at max; this design does not return to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR again absent a new, independently-discovered defect.
